sections.value: # Security verdict, #305 at 52ffd6c: pass The fixes for S303-N1 and S303-N2 are verified, both statically and in a live browser. ## No data reaches markup unescaped - **Static audit of the template.** There are three `innerHTML` sinks: - the empty state (a constant); - the tally (constants plus a count); - `cardHtml`, where every data value now goes through `esc()`, including `colour` in `style=""` and `pr`. Every other data value is set through `textContent` or `setAttribute` (SVG paint). Every colour source (branch, stack, crew `realColour`, label `fill`) comes from `D.lines`/`D.sidings`, which `cleanData` normalises to `#rgb`/`#rrggbb` or `var(--muted)`. Stops are walked recursively: `pr` must be a positive safe integer, and `url` must start with `https://` (no `javascript:` or `data:`). The depot crew colour is the constant `var(--ink)`. - **Attribute contexts.** `esc()` alone does not stop CSS injection inside `style` (mutant M1 below shows it). The colour allow-list is what closes that: in the generator through `COLOUR_RE`, and again on page load through `safeColour`. - **Live test.** Headless Chrome ran on index.html with a hostile `fleet-map.data.js` written directly, so the generator's checks were bypassed and only the page-side layer was tested. The hostile values were: - `colour = red;background:url(https://evil.example/c)">` - `pr = "1"` - `url = javascript:` and `data:text/html` Hovering all 24 data-key elements opened 24 cards. The card HTML contained no ``, no `javascript:` or `data:` link and no `evil.example`, and `window.PWN` was never set. The valid PR #7 still rendered. - **Mutations** (scratch copies of probe.html; all caught): - M1: `cleanData` disabled. The `javascript:` link and the `evil.example` CSS `url()` reach the cards. - M2: M1, plus `esc` removed from colour. `` markup is injected. - M3: M1, plus `esc` removed from pr. `` markup is injected. So each layer carries weight. ## No external requests (S303-N1) - The Google Fonts links are removed, and `` is added. - Static scan: the template contains no `http(s)://` apart from the SVG namespace string, and no `url()` beyond in-page `#ids`. It has no `@import`, `fetch`, XHR, `Image`, `Worker`, `WebSocket`, `sendBeacon` or `location` use. - Chrome net-log of the standalone file: only Chrome's own background traffic (update2, variations, accounts, identical in the control run). There were no font or page-initiated requests. ## gh argv cannot be steered - `execFileSync("gh", ["pr","view",String(n),"-R",repo,...])` runs with no shell. - `n` passes `prOf`, a positive safe integer, so nothing that isn't a number is ever looked up. - `repo` passes `REPO_RE`, which forbids a leading `-` or `.`, so it can't read as a flag or a path step. - The `pij outputs --subject pr:${n}` call uses the same integer. ## C21 The added fixture and test lines use only `example.invalid` and `x.invalid` URLs. No secrets or home paths.
